title: CEO Interview with Paul Butler of VeriQuantix
gist: VeriQuantix, a Silicon Catalyst ChipStart AU startup, is developing Quantum Link Verification (QLV), which uses quantum interference to detect physical tampering on optical fibre and complements post-quantum cryptography. It is still moving from lab prototype toward a compact commercial product, with pilots on carrier networks under discussion.

insights.claim: Encryption protects data contents but does not reveal whether the optical fibre carrying that data has been physically tapped, spliced or diverted, leaving a blind spot in current network security.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Physical-layer link assurance is pitched as a distinct security category to watch alongside cryptography.
insights.quote: encryption protects what’s inside the envelope. QLV tells you whether someone has opened the envelope along the way

insights.claim: The last mile of fibre often runs outside the secure data-centre perimeter through shared conduits, street cabinets and junction boxes, and fibre-tapping equipment is cheap and commercially available, so the barrier to physical eavesdropping is lower than security teams assume.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Suggests demand for physical-layer monitoring at carrier and data-centre edges.
insights.locator: The last mile is often outside the secure perimeter

insights.claim: Harvest-now-decrypt-later turns the quantum threat into a present-day data-collection problem, because adversaries can store encrypted traffic today and decrypt it once quantum computers are powerful enough.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Long data shelf-life supports urgency for both PQC migration and link integrity spending.

insights.claim: VeriQuantix's QLV uses quantum interference between a photon sent over the link and its twin kept locally to continuously detect physical tampering on optical fibre.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Core mechanism of a pre-commercial quantum-security approach.
insights.locator: Your technology sends a photon out and keeps its twin at home

insights.claim: VeriQuantix replaced the need to store a photon for the fibre round-trip time with a locally generated reference, which made the system practical to deploy over kilometres of live fibre while, per the company, keeping the same security guarantees.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The key engineering step the company credits for moving from lab demos to carrier-network pilots.

insights.claim: Taking quantum interference measurements out of the lab means coping with thermal drift, polarization changes and live-network noise, which is the main commercialisation hurdle the CEO describes.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Field robustness, not the science, is the risk factor for quantum-networking startups.
insights.locator: The science of quantum interference has been known for years

insights.claim: QLV is positioned as complementary physical-layer infrastructure beneath NIST post-quantum cryptography rather than a competing standard, so buyers would not have to choose between the two.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Addressable market is additive to the PQC migration spend by enterprises and carriers.

insights.claim: The CEO says enterprises and carriers are already investing heavily in migrating to NIST post-quantum algorithms.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: PQC migration is a live budget line that adjacent security products can attach to.
insights.locator: NIST’s post-quantum algorithms get most of the attention

insights.claim: VeriQuantix's stated five-year goal is to make quantum link verification a standard, unobtrusive layer of network security, starting with turning a lab prototype into a compact, manufacturable commercial product.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Early-stage; treat as aspirational with no revenue or customer data given.
insights.locator: What do you imagine this to be in 5 years’ time?

insights.claim: VeriQuantix joined the 12-month Silicon Catalyst ChipStart AU program to gain mentors and partners for scaling from invention to a deployable product, and says it is now discussing pilots on carrier networks.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Pre-commercial stage; watch for carrier pilot announcements.
insights.locator: Why did you join Silicon Catalyst ChipStart AU
